recipes.name: Old Charleston-Style Shrimp and Grits
ingredients_raw: 2 pounds uncooked shrimp, peeled and deveined
1 pinch cayenne pepper, or to taste
1 pound andouille sausage, cut into 1/4-inch slices

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Bring water and 2 teaspoons salt to a boil in a heavy saucepan over medium-high heat.

Whisk grits into the boiling water, and then whisk in half-and-half. Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer, stirring occasionally, until grits are thickened and tender, 15 to 20 minutes. Set aside and keep warm.
Season shrimp with salt and cayenne pepper. Add lemon juice, toss to combine, and set aside to marinate.
Place sausage slices in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook, stirring occasionally, until browned, 5 to 8 minutes. Remove sausage from the skillet.

Add bacon to the same skillet. Cook over medium-high heat until evenly browned, about 5 minutes per side. Transfer bacon to paper towels to drain, then chop or crumble when cool enough to handle. Leave bacon drippings in the skillet.
Add bell peppers, onion, and garlic to the bacon drippings; cook and stir until onion is translucent, about 8 minutes.
Stir cooked sausage and marinated shrimp into the skillet with the cooked vegetables. Turn off the heat and set aside.

Melt butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in flour, stirring to create a smooth roux. Turn heat to low and cook, stirring constantly, until mixture is golden brown in color, 8 to 10 minutes. Watch carefully, mixture burns easily.
Pour the roux over the sausage, shrimp, and vegetables.
Place the skillet over medium heat, add chicken broth, bacon, and Worcestershire sauce, and stir to combine. Cook until sauce thickens up and shrimp turn opaque and bright pink, about 8 minutes.
Just before serving, mix Cheddar cheese into grits; stir until cheese is melted and grits are creamy and light yellow.
Spoon grits onto plates and serve shrimp mixture over top.

raw_recipe.headline: Old Charleston-Style Shrimp and Grits
raw_recipe.description: This shrimp and grits recipe featuring creamy, cheesy grits topped with a savory shrimp sauce is a classic Southern seafood dish bursting with flavor.

video.description: Send your taste buds to coastal South Carolina with the restaurant-worthy shrimp and grits recipe in this video. Whether you're a beginner cook or a seasoned pro, this top-rated recipe will impress everyone.

review.reviewBody: Shrimp and Grits - a dish that has been nagging me for years to try it. Last week, while in Memphis, I finally tried it and fell in lust. But the dish was VERY spicy and on the greasy side and I knew I could do better. I researched Shrimp and Grits on my flight home and learned a lot, not the least of which was that it was originally a breakfast dish. I also learned there are as many ways to make it as Mama makes her meatballs, and everyone thinks theirs is the true and only way to make it. I say bah! Make what appeals to you - wine, no wine, tomatoes or not, okra, no okra, cream or no. The variations seemed endless. Make what appeals to you - and this recipe appealed to me. It ran circles around the dish I had at a popular restaurant in Memphis (clearly they do much better with barbecue!) and both Hubs and I thought this was "lick-your-plate-clean good." Because it is my preference I used polenta rather than grits, but the difference, really, is marginal. I used chicken broth in the polenta/grits rather than the water simply so as not to waste what I had left. It just contributed a richer flavor anyway! The recipe itself is perfect in my mind. I can't say enough how blown away Hubs and I both were over this. It is traditionally a humble dish, but it is also quite elegant - something I will be sure to keep in mind when I want to impress. Once again, this version of Shrimp and Grits is a real "beaut" and I would suggest following it to the letter. A+

The recipe was easy enough to follow and since I chopped the veggies and gathered all of the ingredients before starting the cooking process, I was able to tend to each detail. And yes, it was totally worth it. It turned out wonderful! The first bite confirmed that this is exactly what I’ve been looking for. The only change I made was that I added 1/4 cup of half and half along with the chicken broth, directly to the roux. I still used the 2 cups of half and half with the grits but felt like I’d have a better roux by adding just a smidge of cream. Simple, yet so elegant and tasty. I will be making this again for our annual Christmas Eve brunch.

A couple of suggestions...
Move Step 7 up to Step 1: You don't want to start making a roux, while your shrimp are already in the pot & cooking.

Flip the order of Steps 3 & 4: The andouille will brown more quickly in the bacon fat, with little chance of sticking.

This dish had very good flavor.

This was so good that I had to create an account to leave my first ever review after years of using this site. I added a can of diced tomatoes, used turkey bacon and chicken andouille, used frozen shrimp, used chicken broth instead of water in the grits, and cajun spice mix instead of any other spices. And despite the substitutions it turned out FABULOUS. No kidding, probably the best dish I have ever made. Takes a bit to make, but is well worth it.

this is probably my favorite recipe from AR so far. I made a few changes, but purely for our tastes. I added a dash of cajun crab boil seasoning to the grits and split the cheese with 1/2 sharp and 1/2 parm. kicked up the veggies and meat with some extra cajun seasoning. you can follow this recipe to the letter and it would be great. we just like a little extra spice.

I made this without modification and found it surprisingly bland. If I were to make it again I would use 2 bell peppers instead of three (I like bell pepper but found WAY too many as written), use Cajun seasoning instead of cayenne on the shrimp, and double the Worcestershire. I did find if you start heating up liquid for your grits (I used broth instead of water) at the same time as you start sautéing the sausage and start your roux when sautéing the veggies the timing works well.

This recipe was to die for!!! I made the following changes trying to make it 'healthier': replaced the andouille sausage with plant-based sausage, cut the half &half with fat free, and eliminated the cheese (why smother the delicious flavor with cheese? IT CAME OUT DELICIOUS!!! My man is scraping the pan!!!! It was a joy to cook. THANK YOU!!

My neice and I have been in search of Low Country Shrimp and Grits. Restaurants in the Midwest disappointed. We both agreed this recipe is a 9.7! The only adjustment was that we added fresh cut sweet corn and the corn milk from that cob to the grits. (scraped the cob after removing the kernels). Total keeper!! Chop the veggies ahead of time. Use high quality stone ground grits. Took about 90 minutes to make, but worth every second!!!

Absolutely outrageously good!!! Made it earlier in the day to recipe, except for green peppers (not a fan) used mini bells in yellow, red and orange instead. Reheated low and slow after adding 1/2 c. ea of water and dry white wine. Devine with the wonderful creamy grits!!

This is my wife’s all time favorite recipe. If followed exactly it will provide a rich, delicious meal that will not disappoint. I recommend prepping the ingredients before beginning because there are a lot of moving parts. I use a stock pot for cooking everything but the grits and roux. This reduces mess for me. I also like to cut the andouille sausage rounds into quarters and brown them this way. It yields crispier bite size pieces that I prefer. Definitely try this recipe and enjoy!

My boyfriend and I both went to school in Charleston for college. He hadnt had shrimp and grits in a year after joining the navy, so I bought a bag of Carolina stone ground grits and brought them with me to California. I cooked him this recipe and it brought a grown man to tears. 

I cut the recipe in half and used extra garlic. They didn’t have andouille in california, so I used kielbasa and doused it in Tabasco. Worked plenty well.
Great recipe as is. Wouldn't change a thing!
I would add a little more flour and cayenne pepper, but tasted really good.
This is staying in my arsenal! Absolutely awesome recipe. Tons of flavor. Rib sticking, hearty meal. Because I like a little extra heat I added some Cajun Two step to the shrimp marinade.
Excellent!
Best Shrimp and Grits we ever had. The only changes I made was LOW SODIUM everything. Yes I still used salt but it was Mortons Lite Salt. It was AWESOME . I will make this again
Takes me back to New Orleans

This recipe is outstanding! We followed it exactly as written and it came out fantastic. While I was eating it, I decided to sprinkle some Old Bay on it just to see if it enhanced the already great taste. It did! You certainly don't have to do that but it did add some extra flavor. I will absolutely be making this again. My girlfriend and I had a few drinks while making this and didn't realize the recipe was for 8 people. There was a lot left over but I'm sure the leftovers will be gone quickly.
I made the gravy while sausage was in the pan. It turned out Very good! I will make it again.
Followed the recipe and it turned out great. Ready to serve guests next time!
